findings.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:150 — The second downsize definition replaces the first because Ruby does not overload methods by signature, causing existing three-argument calls to raise ArgumentError and two-argument calls to treat height as the options hash and fail at opts[:allow_animation].

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — The unconditional 10 MB limit overrides the configured upload limit for non-image attachments, rejecting previously valid uploads on sites allowing attachments larger than 10 MB.

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment: the downsize method is defined twice in Ruby, and since Ruby doesn't support method overloading, the second definition overrides/replaces the first. Both comments point out that this breaks existing code that calls the method with the original signature (separate width and height arguments). The candidate even provides more specific technical details about the consequences (ArgumentError, treating height as options hash).

per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — The unconditional 10 MB limit overrides the configured upload limit for non-image attachments, rejecting previously valid uploads on sites allowing attachments larger than 10 MB.
per_golden_matches.reasoning: Both comments identify the same issue: the hardcoded 10 MB (10 * 1024 KB) limit ignores the configurable site settings for upload limits. The golden comment specifically mentions that maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], while the candidate comment says the unconditional 10 MB limit overrides the configured upload limit. Both are pointing to the same problem - hardcoded values diverging from server-side/configurable settings.
